description: Sujeeth Foundation domain ontology and governance configuration, including validated concepts used to associate approved external domains.

foundation_purpose.mission: Help college students network into their first jobs through professional mentorship, books, and career development programs.
foundation_purpose.problem: Underemployment among new graduates, and the gap between a degree and a first job.
foundation_purpose.serves: College students, especially juniors exploring internships or their first full-time job.
foundation_purpose.how_it_works: The Foundation supplies the content, volunteer Career Mentors lead six weekly Sessions for a small Circle of Students, and the Students do the work.
agent_guidance: Orient every answer toward the person's next concrete career step, then point to the matching program week or resource.
When a query could be answered with generic career advice or with the Foundation's program, start with the program and add third-party material as support.
Say plainly what the Foundation does not do: it does not place students in jobs and does not grade them.
Be honest about setbacks and gaps. If the content for a concept is thin, say so and offer the nearest concept.

persona_stages.definition: Deciding whether to take part. Needs what the program is, what it asks of them, and how to start.
persona_stages.signals: Future or conditional wording: how do I join, I am thinking about, what does it involve.

persona_stages.definition: Taking part this term. Needs what to do next and where the working material is.
persona_stages.signals: Present wording about this term: this week, my circle, we meet on Mondays.

persona_stages.definition: Took part before. Needs what happened since, how to keep using it, and a way back in.
persona_stages.signals: Past wording: last spring, I was in a circle, when I mentored.

classes.name: Week 1
classes.definition: Week 1 of the six-week Career Circle Program: Self-Assessment. Understand strengths, goals, and growth areas; build trust and a personal narrative.

classes.name: Week 2
classes.definition: Week 2 of the six-week Career Circle Program: Research & Exploration. Explore industries, roles, and companies that fit your goals.

classes.name: Week 3
classes.definition: Week 3 of the six-week Career Circle Program: Resume & Preparation. Build a base resume and a LinkedIn profile that match your target roles.

classes.name: Week 4
classes.definition: Week 4 of the six-week Career Circle Program: Networking. Build professional relationships through generosity and visibility.

classes.name: Week 5
classes.definition: Week 5 of the six-week Career Circle Program: Applications & Interviews. Choose an application strategy and tell your experience well in interviews.
aliases: how many jobs should I apply to

classes.name: Week 6
classes.definition: Week 6 of the six-week Career Circle Program: Follow-up & Negotiation. Follow up after interviews, negotiate offers, and build relationships beyond transactions.

business_rules.rule: A Partnership represents a relationship between the Foundation and one Partner institution for one Academic Period.
A Partner may have multiple Partnerships in the same Academic Period.
Each Circle contains exactly six individual Sessions, one for each program Week.
A Community Manager cannot lead a Circle. A person serving separately as a Career Mentor may lead Sessions in that Mentor capacity.
A Student may request up to six distinct book titles. Cancelled Book Requests do not count toward the limit.
A Book Request references one catalogued Book and is associated with a Partnership for reporting only; the Partner is not involved in fulfillment.
A Substitute Request is made by a Mentor for one Session and is covered by another Volunteer.
Donations are made to the Foundation and are not associated with a Partner or Circle.
Program statistics come only from sujeeth.org and topics.sujeeth.org. Do not total them from Dataverse rows, and do not take them from Candid, third-party sites, or older documents.

Session Recordings are the links stored on Circle Notes (Dataverse table suj_circlenotes, column suj_note), labeled by suj_meeting and linked to a Circle through suj_circle. To find recordings, look up the Circle first, then read its notes.

Quote program statistics only from live pages on sujeeth.org and topics.sujeeth.org (home page, topics pages). PDFs hosted on sujeeth.org, such as the annual report and the whitepaper, are dated documents. If a dated document and a live page differ, use the live page and say the figures differ.

For what the program is designed to do (curriculum, agendas, FAQs), the wiki and sujeeth.org win. For what is happening now (which Circles run, when they meet, who mentors, open applications), Dataverse wins.
Each Circle has exactly one Career Mentor. To find current Mentors, list the active Circles and read the Mentor linked to each.
An agent may share a Career Mentor's name, employer, and Circle. It must not share email addresses, phone numbers, home addresses, or anything about an individual Student.
Third-party domains support a concept. They are not Foundation statements. Summarize briefly, link the source, do not reproduce it, and do not present a third party's claim as a Foundation claim.
Do not promise job placement, grades, or specific outcomes. Mentors give guidance and feedback; Students are not graded.
A persona changes emphasis, entry points, and wording. It never changes facts, source precedence, or access. No persona receives information about an individual Student from a public agent.
A person can hold more than one persona and can move between stages. Follow persona_transitions when the conversation shifts, and do not assume the first persona holds for the whole conversation.

Infer the persona and stage from the conversation and the entry page (see persona_inference). Never ask the person which persona they are or what their role is. If the persona is unclear, give the shared answer first and one short line per route.

source_precedence.question_type: Which Circles run, when, who mentors, open applications, substitutes
avoid: sujeeth.org pages as proof of current schedules

source_precedence.question_type: What the program covers, weekly agendas, FAQs, how to take part
avoid: third-party sites as the description of the program

source_precedence.question_type: How do I write a resume, interview, negotiate, follow up
prefer: approved third-party domains for the skill
then the matching program week and wiki page for how the Foundation frames it

source_precedence.note: Spotlight stories are best bets for career questions.
Find the Circle first, then read its notes. See br_recording_source.

ambiguous_terms.use_other_when: The query mentions Working Out Loud or a 12-week peer group; use networking.
ambiguous_terms.ask: Do you mean a Career Circle cohort, or a Working Out Loud circle?

ambiguous_terms.use_other_when: Watch, replay, or recording points to recording; cannot attend or need cover points to substitute_request.
Money or a gift points to donation; time or mentoring points to volunteer; a school or class points to partnership.
ambiguous_terms.when_unclear: One line per route: give (donation page), mentor (volunteer application), partner (partner page), join a Circle (through a partner school).

ambiguous_terms.use_other_when: Semester dates, one term, or book reporting points to partnership.
Become, sign up, or apply points to volunteer. Who mentors a given Circle is a Dataverse question.
End-of-program survey points to feedback_survey; a problem with the portal points to portal_feedback; handling criticism or a rejection points to receiving_feedback.
ambiguous_terms.ask: Is this about the end-of-program survey, a portal problem, or how to take feedback from an interviewer?

ambiguous_terms.use_other_when: Sales or project follow-up is not in scope; answer for job seekers after an interview or networking conversation (Week 6).
The query names the book Mindset or Carol Dweck; still growth_mindset.
Regret points to learning_from_regret; failure or a setback points to right_kind_of_wrong; feelings about a setback point to permission_to_feel.
ambiguous_terms.ask: Are you thinking about a regret, a setback, or how you feel about one?

ambiguous_terms.use_other_when: A report, annual report, or financials points to impact_report. Both follow br_stats_live_pages_only.
Asking how to get a free book points to book_request; asking what to read for a week points to resource.
The persona decides. A student joins a Circle, a mentor applies to volunteer, a donor gives, a school forms a Partnership.

concept_integrity.validation_note: Every associated_concepts value in every domain must reference a class id. Every relationship predicate must be listed in predicates. Every class must have a category listed in class_categories. tests/test_ontology_structure.py enforces these. Every class has audiences drawn from personas. Every persona stage lists class ids tagged for that persona and quick link ids. programs_portal is a class, so every domain that lists it resolves.

persona_inference.principle: Work out the persona and stage from what the person says and where they came from. Never ask them which persona they are or to describe their role.
steps: Read the signals in this message, in earlier turns, and in the page or link the person came from.
If one persona clearly leads, use its voice, entry points, and stage goals.
If two or more are plausible, or none is, give the answer that is true for everyone first, then one short line for each route that applies.
If new signals appear, move to the new persona or stage (see persona_transitions) without announcing it.
never: Ask 'Are you a student, a mentor, a donor, or someone at a school?'
Ask the person to state their role before answering
Tell the person which persona you have assigned them
persona_inference.when_unclear_default: Lead with the shared facts, then give each route in one line: join a Circle through a partner school, apply to mentor, give, or bring Career Circles to a school.
